title: Automated Segmentation of Intrinsic Foot Muscles in Ultrasound Using Deep Neural Networks: Development and Validation Study.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate the first automated deep-learning image-processing framework for pixel-level segmentation of the plantar intrinsic foot muscles (PIMs) in ultrasound (US) images. This approach supports objective and reproducible US-based muscle segmentation from conventional B-mode images. Methods US images of four PIMs (abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis (FDB), quadratus plantae [QP] and abductor digiti minimi) were collected from 200 healthy participants (n = 1099 images). Manual segmentations were used as ground truth. Three deep neural network architectures (U-Net, Feature Pyramid Network [FPN] and DeepLabV3+) with a Mix Transformer backbone were trained and evaluated. Model performance was assessed using the Intersection over Union (IoU) and Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), two complementary pixel-level segmentation metrics. Agreement with manual measurements was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), mean difference and standard error of measurement. Results All models demonstrated excellent segmentation performance, with mean IoU values ≥0.90 and mean DSC values ≥0.95 across all muscles. The highest accuracy was observed for the FDB (IoU = 0.95; DSC = 0.97), while QP showed slightly lower performance (IoU = 0.90; DSC = 0.95). FPN and DeepLabV3+ exhibited greater stability (SD: ±0.02-0.03) compared to U-Net (up to ±0.08). Agreement with manual segmentation was high for cross-sectional area (ICC: 0.836-0.960) and moderate-to-high for border length (ICC: 0.705-0.944), with minimal systematic bias. Mean model inference time was under 0.01 s per image, reflecting forward-pass model inference only and excluding image loading, resizing and post-processing. Conclusion This study presents the first automated segmentation framework for the PIMs in US. Built on established segmentation architectures with a Mix Transformer backbone, it enables accurate and reliable pixel-level segmentation in under 0.01 s per image; its novelty lies in extending automated musculoskeletal US analysis to this previously unaddressed muscle group. By automating tissue boundary detection at the pixel level, this framework advances US imaging beyond conventional manual measurement, enabling objective and scalable musculoskeletal assessment with reduced operator dependence at the segmentation stage. These findings establish the feasibility of accurate and reproducible PIM segmentation in healthy adults and provide the necessary foundation for subsequent validation in clinical populations.

title: Deep Learning-Enabled Automated B-mode Segmentation for Regional Cerebral Perfusion Assessment in Neonates Using Ultrafast Power Doppler.
abstract: Cerebral perfusion disturbances contribute to neonatal brain injury, and ultrafast power Doppler can quantify regional cerebral blood volume but relies on manual segmentation that limits clinical use. We developed and validated a U-Net model for automated regional brain segmentation on B-mode images derived from neonatal transfontanellar ultrafast ultrasound to enable rapid arterial and venous cerebral blood volume quantification. Time-integrated, log-compressed ultrafast B-mode images from 80 neonates were manually segmented by an expert into the cortico-sub-cortical areas, the cingulate gyrus and the basal ganglia, and then used to train a U-Net with class-weighted loss (a 70/15/15 train/validation/test split). The trained model was then applied to segment B-mode images, with the resulting regions of interest used to quantify arterial and venous cerebral blood volume from the corresponding power Doppler data. Segmentation performance was quantified using the Dice similarity coefficient, with agreement between artificial intelligence- and manually derived cerebral blood volume assessed by Bland-Altman analysis. The median Dice similarity coefficients were 83%, 84% and 88% for the three regions. Mean Bland-Altman differences were ≤0.103 dB (arterial) and ≤0.096 dB (venous). Perturbation of the predicted masks by ±35% surface area change showed the narrowest limits of agreement at the unperturbed prediction, changing by no more than 0.1 dB between -5% and +5%, demonstrating automated segmentation as a rapid, reproducible alternative to manual delineation.

title: Automated Quantification of 3-D Carotid Ultrasound Vessel Wall Texture Change Predicts Vascular Events.
abstract: Objective To reduce reliance on labor-intensive and operator-dependent explicit plaque segmentation, we evaluated whether a texture-change score (ΔTexture) derived from semi-automated 3-D ultrasound (3-DUS) vessel wall segmentation predicts vascular events better than baseline vessel wall texture (BL-Texture), vessel wall volume change (ΔVWV) and Framingham risk score. Methods 3-DUS images were acquired from 272 patients with carotid atherosclerosis at baseline and 1 y later. Vessel walls were delineated using a validated, minimally user-initialized segmentation workflow. Longitudinal texture change was summarized as vessel wall ΔTexture and compared with BL-Texture, ΔVWV and Framingham risk score. Patients were followed for up to 5 y (median, 3.16 y) for myocardial infarction, transient ischemic attack and stroke. Results ΔTexture and BL-Texture predicted vascular events (log-rank, p < 0.001 for both), whereas ΔVWV did not. No event occurred in the lowest-risk tertile of ΔTexture. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of ΔTexture was 0.89, compared with 0.82 for BL-Texture, 0.53 for ΔVWV and 0.53 for Framingham risk score. In Cox regression, ΔTexture (median hazard ratio, 4.05; p < 0.001) and BL-Texture (median hazard ratio, 3.63; p < 0.001) were significant predictors, whereas ΔVWV and Framingham risk score were not. Conclusion Vessel wall ΔTexture derived from minimally user-initialized 3-DUS vessel wall segmentation predicted vascular events better than ΔVWV and Framingham risk score. This approach provides a scalable imaging biomarker for vascular event risk assessment without requiring explicit plaque segmentation.

title: Doppler-based Radiomics Integrated With Frozen Section Analysis Enhances Borderline Ovarian Tumor Prediction: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Objective To develop a Doppler-based radiomics model that utilizes tumor characteristics related to neovascularization, with or without integrating intraoperative frozen section analysis (FSA), to enhance borderline ovarian tumors (BOT) prediction. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, patients diagnosed with BOT or epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) between January 2010 and October 2022 across five centers were included. Data from Center I were randomly divided into training (80%) and validation (20%) sets, while Centers II-V provided the test set. Three ultrasound-radiomics models were developed: color Doppler features (CD), grayscale features (GS), and combining both (GSCD). An Integration Model was developed by incorporating clinical variables, FSA and the best-performing radiomics model. Color Doppler signals were acquired through three channels with RGB information. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results A total of 1244 patients with a median age of 49 years (IQR, 37-58 years) were included, consisting of 520 patients with BOT and 724 EOC. The GSCD exhibited the best predictive performance for BOT among the three ultrasound-radiomics models, showing an AUC of 0.975 (95%CI, 0.962-0.985) in the training set, with a sensitivity of 92.9% and a specificity of 88.9% in the validation set. The Integration Model further improved the performance, achieving an AUC of 0.997 (95%CI, 0.993-0.998) in the training set, with a sensitivity of 87.2% and a specificity of 98.7% in the validation set. Additionally, both the GSCD and Integration Model effectively distinguished BOT from Stage I EOC, with AUCs of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.849-0.963) and 0.936 (95% CI: 0.871-0.974) in the validation set. Conclusion We developed a Doppler-based radiomics model utilizing red-green-blue information. This model, irrespective of integration with FSA, demonstrated improved accuracy in predicting BOT and stratified the FIGO Stage EOC.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Multimodal Integration of Ultrasound and CT for Identifying Central Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the utility of multimodal imaging biomarkers in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), this study developed a deep learning model using ultrasound (US) and computed tomography (CT) imaging to predict central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in PTC by integrating radiomic features of perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) at the cervical vertebra 6 (C6) level. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 477 PTC patients from two centers. Using ResNet101 with Hierarchical Attention Integration (ResHAI-101), we extracted deep learning features of the tumor area from US images. Separately, we extracted radiomic features of PVAT from CT images. Univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted based on clinical data, followed by feature selection and integration. Results Multimodal prediction model performance was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Predictive performance was validated using an external test cohort (ETC). The Multimodal Prediction Model 3, integrating deep learning features, PVAT radiomic features and clinical features, showed superior diagnostic performance for predicting CLNM compared to the Unimodal Model, achieving AUCs of 0.915 in the internal test cohort and 0.890 in the ETC. Binary logistic regression identified gender, age, tumor size and extrathyroidal extension as independent risk factors for CLNM. Conclusion This study establishes and validates the significant impact of PVAT on CLNM in PTC, providing a non-invasive tool for pre-operative risk assessment to aid in surgical decision-making.

title: Ultrasound Localization Microscopy Combined With Regional Division for Differentiating Benign and Metastatic Lymph Nodes.
abstract: Objective Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables high-resolution visualization of lymph node microvasculature. However, most previous studies rely on whole-node analysis, which may overlook spatial heterogeneity and be affected by confounding factors. This prospective single-center study aimed to investigate the diagnostic value of ULM combined with regional analysis for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes. Methods A total of 104 lymph nodes from patients with sonographically suspicious lymph nodes were included. All lymph nodes underwent ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy, which served as the reference standard for classification (benign or metastatic). Each lymph node was divided into central, peripheral, and global regions, and ULM quantitative parameters were extracted. Regional ratio features were calculated. Feature selection was performed using univariate analysis, LASSO regression, and backward stepwise logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold stratified cross-validation, 2000 bootstrap resamples, decision curve analysis (DCA), and clinical impact curve (CIC). Results Three diagnostic models were constructed: a conventional ultrasound (US) model, a ULM model, and a combined US-ULM model. The combined model demonstrated the best discriminative performance with an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI: 0.7875-0.9320), followed by the ULM model (AUC = 0.833, 95% CI: 0.7464-0.9108) and the US model (AUC = 0.730, 95% CI: 0.6219-0.8285). In multivariable analysis, SD.Density_C_P (OR =0.0578, p = 0.012), FD_C_P (OR = 0.8847 per 0.01 increase, p = 0.003), and peripheral vascular pattern (OR = 10.9501, p < 0.001) were identified as significant predictors of lymph node metastasis. At optimal cut-off values, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 0.733 and specificity of 0.915. Conclusion The proposed region-based ULM model combined with conventional ultrasound provides an improved quantitative approach for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes in patients with sonographically suspicious lymphadenopathy.

title: Research Progress of Low-Intensity Pulsed Ultrasound in Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder where current pharmacological and surgical interventions, including Deep Brain Stimulation, often fail to reverse neuronal degeneration or halt disease progression. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) has emerged as a novel, non-invasive neuromodulation technology with significant therapeutic potential. This review synthesizes current research on the key acoustic parameters, biological mechanisms, and clinical applications of LIPUS in PD. Unlike High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU), which relies on thermal ablation to destroy target nuclei (e.g., Vim, STN), LIPUS utilizes low-energy mechanical waves (typically <3 W/cm²) to exert non-thermal regulatory effects without damaging tissue. Mechanisms of action include the modulation of mechanosensitive ion channels (e.g., Piezo1), enhancement of neuroplasticity via brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), promotion of autophagy, and regulation of microglial phenotypes to reduce neuroinflammation. We further compare LIPUS with HIFU, highlighting the superiority of LIPUS regarding safety, reversibility, and the absence of requirement for MRI-based thermal monitoring. While preliminary clinical studies using wearable LIPUS devices indicate improvements in motor and cognitive functions, a unified consensus on optimal stimulation parameters and targeting strategies is lacking. Future research should focus on large-scale, standardized clinical trials to establish precise protocols for LIPUS as a disease-modifying therapy for PD.

title: Perilesional biopsy in - systematic out? Comparative analysis of targeted, perilesional and systematic core yield by needle tracking with robotic-assisted transperineal MRI/US fusion prostate biopsy.
abstract: Objectives To characterize prostate cancer (Pca) detection rates by Gleason Grade Group (GG) in targeted, perilesional, and systematic cores sampling the remaining prostate using robotic-assisted transperineal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) /ultrasound fusion biopsy (RA-TP-FBx), enabling precise spatial documentation of every core relative to MRI-lesions and the prostate. Methods We analyzed prospectively collected RA-TP-FBx cases between 2020 and 2024. Biopsies were performed with the iSR'obot Mona Lisa (Biobot). Sampling included a traditional targeted + systematic strategy and a Trizonal approach: targeted + perilesional + systematic. Perilesional cores were defined at biopsy as samples within 10 mm of the MRI-lesion margin and systematic cores as samples outside the targeted-perilesional areas. Individualized 3D prostate maps were correlated with per-core histopathology. Clinically significant PCa (csPCa) was defined as GG ≥ 2. Results The full cohort included 566 RA-TP-FBx cases. Diagnosis of csPCa (n=131 in the Trizonal cohort) was exclusively due to perilesional sampling in 6.1% (8/131). Systematic biopsy detected csPCa not captured by targeted or perilesional cores in 3.8% (5/131), but only 1.5% (2/131) originated from MRI-negative lobes. Overdetection of GG 1 (n = 58 in the Trizonal cohort) would be reduced by 24.1% (14/58) by omitting systematic cores when targeted and perilesional cores were negative. Conclusions Robotic-assisted mapping demonstrated that perilesional sampling effectively complemented targeted biopsy, while systematic cores yielded minimal additional csPCa detection but increased GG 1 overdetection. These data support adopting targeted + perilesional sampling and omitting or deintensifying the routine addition of systematic cores in the remaining prostate.

title: Integrated molecular, immunological, oxidative stress, and histopathological evaluation of Ascaridia galli infection in chickens.
abstract: Ascaridia galli (A. galli) is an important intestinal nematode of chickens, but the host immune, oxidative, and pathological responses associated with natural infection remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to provide an integrated molecular, immunological, oxidative, and histopathological evaluation of naturally occurring A. galli infection in Baladi chickens in Cairo, Egypt. A total of 200 Baladi chickens from farmers' households in rural areas of Cairo Governorate were examined between January and June 2026. Gastrointestinal helminths were recovered and identified, and 40 adult nematodes were subjected to molecular confirmation by amplification and bidirectional sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer-1 (ITS-1) region. Phylogenetic analysis was performed to assess the identity of the recovered isolate. Cytokine gene expression and intestinal oxidative stress were evaluated in infected and non-infected birds. Expression of IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TGF-β, and IFN-γ was quantified by real-time PCR in five birds per group, while intestinal malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), reduced glutathione (GSH), and catalase (CAT) were assessed as oxidative and antioxidant markers. After serological and molecular screening for concurrent infections, six infected and six non-infected chickens that were free from evidence of other infections were selected for histopathological examination, lesion scoring, intestinal morphometry, and TNF-α immunohistochemistry. A. galli was detected in 90 of 200 chickens, giving an overall prevalence of 45% ((95% CI: 38.1-52.1%). The obtained ITS-1 sequence (GenBank accession PZ363554) clustered within the A. galli clade and showed 99.57-100% nucleotide identity with reference A. galli sequences. Compared with controls, infected birds showed significant upregulation of IL-6 (28.8-fold), IL-8 (30.5-fold), IL-10 (55.9-fold), TGF-β (7.8-fold), and IFN-γ (2.2-fold), with IL-10 showing the greatest increase. Intestinal MDA and NO increased 1.44- and 1.80-fold, respectively, whereas GSH and CAT decreased to 0.76- and 0.28-fold of control levels. Histopathology revealed marked villous degeneration, sloughing and shortening, glandular degeneration, fibrosis, muscular hypertrophy, vascular alterations, and inflammatory cell infiltration. TNF-α immunoreactivity was increased in infected tissues, and morphometric analysis demonstrated alterations in villus dimensions, crypt depth, and the villus-to-crypt ratio. Natural A. galli infection was therefore associated with molecularly confirmed parasitism, altered inflammatory and regulatory cytokine expression, intestinal oxidative imbalance, and pronounced tissue injury in Baladi chickens. This work provides a foundation for experimental studies designed to unravel the causal relationships among these endpoints.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of AI in Breast Cancer Screening and Lung Cancer Diagnostics: A Case Study From Costa Rica.
abstract: Objectives This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into breast and lung cancer diagnostic workflows in Costa Rica, addressing the scarcity of health economic evidence for AI adoption in low- and middle-income countries and focusing on context-specific systemic barriers. Methods Two state-transition Markov models compared AI-assisted workflows (AI as a first reader) with conventional radiologist-only strategies over a 10-year horizon. AI-supported mammography screening was evaluated in asymptomatic women aged 50 to 70 years. For lung cancer, symptom-driven pathways were modeled using GLOBOCAN 2022 incidence data. Inputs included region-specific costs (USD), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and progression probabilities, calibrated to Costa Rica's cancer registry. Methodological rigor adhered to the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 guidelines. Results AI in breast cancer screening demonstrated economic dominance: it improved QALYs by 49% (10.46 vs 7.04) and reduced costs by 49% (USD 93 102 vs USD 183 278), yielding a net monetary benefit of USD 212 119 at Costa Rica's willingness-to-pay threshold. For lung cancer, the AI strategy also proved dominant: it reduced total costs to USD 1 218 507 (vs USD 1 337 640) while increasing QALYs to 6.88 (vs 4.15), driven by earlier detection that averts expensive late-stage palliative care. Conclusions AI significantly improved cost-effectiveness in both breast and lung cancer diagnostics, demonstrating economic dominance by mitigating diagnostic delays and reducing late-stage treatment burdens. These findings stress AI's context-dependent impact in low- and middle-income countries and the necessity of early detection investments and equity-focused implementation to align innovation with healthcare system realities.

title: Intestinal ultrasound findings and their prognostic value in patients with eosinophilic gastroenteritis.
abstract: Objective Eosinophilic gastroenteritis (EoGE) is a chronic recurrent disorder with elevated eosinophilic infiltration in the gastrointestinal tract. Objective predictors for disease outcomes are lacking. This study aimed to explore the predictive value of baseline intestinal ultrasound (IUS) along with clinical and laboratory characteristics for disease outcomes. Materials and methods This retrospective cohort study enrolled consecutive patients diagnosed with EoGE at a tertiary medical center between 2019 and 2024. Baseline clinical, laboratory, endoscopy data were collected. IUS images were blindly reviewed for features such as disease location, bowel wall thickness, the "piano key sign" (thickened jejunal folds), and ascites. The primary outcome was steroid-free clinical remission at 12 months. Logistic regression analysis was conducted to reveal the predictive factors. Results This cohort comprised 40 patients with a median age of 34.0 years (IQR, 26.8-52.0 years) and 23 (57.5%) were males. The predominant clinical symptoms included abdominal pain (92.5%), vomiting (52.5%) and diarrhea (47.5%). On IUS, 26 (65.0%) patients showed thickened bowel wall between 4 and 7 mm and predominantly localized in the jejunum (42.5%) and ileum (45.0%). The piano key sign was observed in 12 (30.0%) patients, and ascites was present in 17 (42.5%). Steroid-free clinical remission at 12 months was achieved by 15 (37.5%) patients. On multivariable analysis, the piano key sign (OR 0.092, 95%CI 0.009-0.978, P = 0.048) and vomiting (OR 0.088, 95%CI: 0.017-0.462, P = 0.004) were identified as negative predictors of steroid-free clinical remission with statistical significance, with a combined area under the curve of 0.860. Conclusion The piano key sign on IUS was the negative predictor of steroid-free clinical remission. IUS may provide prognostic information for making personalized treatment and monitoring strategies in EoGE patients.

title: Surgical Anatomy of a Markedly Developed Rhomboid Lip During Cerebellopontine Angle Meningioma Resection: Radiological and Histopathological Correlation.
abstract: Objective The rhomboid lip (RL) is a variable sheet-like neural structure extending from the lateral recess of the fourth ventricle into the cerebellopontine angle (CPA). This technical note describes the radiological, microsurgical, and histopathological features of a markedly developed RL encountered during CPA meningioma surgery, with emphasis on its intraoperative identification and selective surgical management. Methods A 60-year-old woman underwent retrosigmoid resection of a 12-mm left CPA meningioma. Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging suggested a well-developed RL extending from the foramen of Luschka toward the internal auditory canal. Intraoperatively, the RL was assessed according to its morphological features and anatomical relationships and was preserved or selectively divided according to the exposure required during tumor removal. RL tissue that required division for surgical exposure was subsequently examined histopathologically. Results The RL appeared thicker and less transparent than the arachnoid, with veins coursing along its surface. Its relationship with cranial nerve IX and the choroid plexus provided useful anatomical landmarks for identification. The portion overlying the vestibulocochlear nerve was preserved during most of the tumor dissection and divided only when additional exposure was required for complete tumor removal. Histopathological examination demonstrated ependymal and glial layers, confirming the structure as RL. Simpson grade II resection was achieved without new cranial nerve deficits. Conclusions A well-developed RL can be recognized as a distinct anatomical structure using morphological and anatomical landmarks. During CPA surgery, selective preservation or division according to the evolving operative corridor may facilitate anatomically informed surgical dissection.

title: Imaging And Outcomes In The Treatment Of Sacral Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas.
abstract: Objective Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) in the sacral region are extremely rare and their intradural retrograde draining system has not been investigated in detail. The aim of this study was to characterize the venous drainage patterns of sacral DAVFs based on our clinical experience in treating patients with this condition. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sacral DAVFs treated at our institution from January 2016 to January 2024. Preoperative spinal angiography was used to evaluate the positional relationship between the shunt point of sacral DAVF and the vertebral midline. We proposed that if the location of the shunt point was located on the midline, the draining vein would be the filum terminale vein (FTV); if the shunt point was located off the midline, the draining vein would be the radiculomedullary vein (RMV). Results A total of 17 sacral DAVFs patients treated with direct surgery were included in this study. All patients presented with lower extremity weakness and numbness. Sphincter dysfunction was present in 15 patients (88.2%). The mean interval from symptom onset to diagnosis was 14.1 months (range 1-96 months). Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging(MRI) detected T2 hyperintensity at the level of the conus medullaris and intradural flow voids in all patients. Spinal angiography confirmed the diagnosis of sacral DAVF in all cases, and complete fistula occlusion was achieved with surgical ligation in all patients. Intraoperatively, 4 patients with the midline location of the shunt point were confirmed to have FTV as the draining vein, while the other 13 patients with off-midline shunt point were confirmed to have RMV as the draining vein. The intraoperative findings were completely consistent with the preoperative assessment of the draining veins based on the location of the shunt point. Conclusions The draining veins of sacral DAVFs are not always the FTVs, in fact, most sacral DAVFs drain via the RMV. With our simple imaging-based method, the two different types of draining veins in sacral DAVFs can be preliminarily identified before surgery.

title: Classification of Vertebral Artery Course Variations in the Atlantoaxial Region and Their Anatomic Considerations for Surgical Planning: A CTA Imaging Analysis of 511 Patients.
abstract: Background Vertebral artery (VA) course variations in the atlantoaxial region pose significant risks during posterior C1-C2 fixation. This study aimed to classify these variations on CT angiography (CTA) and assess their anatomic implications for surgical planning. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 511 patients (1,022 vertebral arteries) who underwent cervical CTA at Beijing Tongren Hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Vertebral artery course variations were classified by two independent senior radiologists. Interobserver agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa coefficient. Associations between variation types and gender/side were analyzed using chi-square tests with adjusted standardized residuals. potential surgical implications were assessed based on anatomical relationships and literature review Results: Seven types were identified: normal type (712 arteries, 70%), high-riding type (243, 24%), posterior arch bridge type (26, 2.5%), protruding type (14, 1.4%), segmental artery type (13, 1.2%), fenestration type (9, 0.9%), and combined type (5, 0.5%). Interobserver agreement was substantial (κ = 0.795). Each type carries distinct anatomic considerations for screw placement, exposure, and surgical approach selection. Conclusions Different vertebral artery course variation types carry distinct and predictable potential surgical implications. Detailed preoperative CTA assessment with three-dimensional reconstruction is essential for identifying these variations and minimizing the risk of iatrogenic vertebral artery injury during posterior atlantoaxial surgery.

Conclusions

Different vertebral artery course variation types carry distinct and predictable potential surgical implications. Detailed preoperative CTA assessment with three-dimensional reconstruction is essential for identifying these variations and minimizing the risk of iatrogenic vertebral artery injury during posterior atlantoaxial surgery.

title: MRI-Only Preoperative Localization and Semiautomated Three-Dimensional Modeling of the Cervical Vagus Nerve for Vagus Nerve Stimulation Implantation.
abstract: Background We evaluated whether three-dimensional steady-state free precession with time-spatial labeling inversion pulse (3D-SSFP with time-SLIP) MRI could localize the cervical vagus nerve before vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) implantation and developed training-data-free semiautomated vagus nerve tracking software. Methods Thirty patients with drug-resistant epilepsy underwent preoperative cervical 3D-SSFP with time-SLIP MRI followed by VNS implantation. The left vagus nerve was visually identified at the planned surgical level, and its relationship to the common carotid artery (CCA) and internal jugular vein (IJV) was classified. MRI localization was validated against intraoperative findings. A MATLAB-based tool semi-automatically tracked the vagus nerve, CCA, and IJV from user-defined reference points. Accuracy was assessed using coordinate error and classification agreement. Results The vagus nerve was identified on MRI in all 30 patients, with complete concordance between MRI and intraoperative localization. Among 29 classifiable patients, the nerve was located superficially between the CCA and IJV in 45%, superficially and lateral to the CCA in 41%, deep between the CCA and IJV in 10%, and deep and medial to the CCA in 3.4%. The median distance between software-derived and visually identified coordinates was 1 mm (interquartile range, 1-2 mm), and software-derived classification agreed with consensus visual classification in 27 of 29 patients (93%). Conclusions Cervical MRI enabled preoperative localization of the vagus nerve and adjacent vessels. The semiautomated method showed close agreement with expert visual assessment and may support anatomical orientation and surgical planning for VNS implantation.

title: Image-guided focused ultrasound for non-invasive modulation of superficial and deep tissues.
abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) enables non-invasive, spatially precise modulation of biological tissues. This protocol describes assembly, calibration, and implementation of a diagnostic ultrasound-guided FUS (dUS-FUS) platform for real-time targeting of superficial and deep tissues in small-animal models. We demonstrate reversible sciatic nerve modulation in a rat acute pain model and assess sensory and motor functions using behavioral tests. The platform provides a reproducible workflow for image-guided tissue modulation and can be adapted to diverse preclinical applications. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Sangwan et al. 1 , 2 .

title: ADHD symptom positivity and its association with medication adherence and psychiatric burden in adults with epilepsy.
abstract: Background Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms are increasingly recognized in adults with epilepsy (AwE) and may contribute to psychiatric burden, seizure-related outcomes, and treatment adherence. We therefore investigated the frequency of ADHD symptom positivity and its associations with medication adherence, psychiatric symptoms, seizure burden, and neurophysiological findings. Methods This cross-sectional study included 100 AwE and 94 healthy controls. ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS-v1.1). Anxiety and depressive symptoms were evaluated using the Beck Anxiety Inventory and Beck Depression Inventory, respectively. Medication adherence was assessed using the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8). Participants were classifiedas ASRS-positive or ASRS-negative according to the six-item ASRS Part A screener. Clinical, psychiatric, electroencephalographic, and magnetic resonance imaging findings were compared between groups. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with ADHD-symptom-positivity. Results ADHD-symptom-positivity was significantly more frequent in AwE than in healthy controls (50.0% vs. 25.5%, p = 0.001). Within the epilepsy cohort, ASRS-positive participants demonstrated lower medication adherence (p = 0.010), higher rates of poor adherence (70.0% vs. 48.0%, p = 0.042), higher anxiety (p = 0.002), and depression scores (p < 0.001). Clinically significant anxiety and depression were also more common among ASRS-positive participants (p = 0.027 and p < 0.001, respectively). In multivariable analysis, depression score was independently associated with ADHD-symptom-positivity (OR = 1.147, 95% CI 1.039-1.267, p = 0.007). Conclusions ADHD-symptom-positivity is common in AwE and is associated with poorer medication adherence in the between-group analysis, but this association did not remain statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, while greater psychiatric symptom burden was observed. Routine screening for ADHD-related symptoms may facilitate identification of adults with epilepsy at increased riskfor adverse clinical outcomes and support more comprehensive epilepsy care.

title: Adult aphasic status epilepticus: A systematic review and patient-level synthesis of clinical phenotypes and multimodal diagnostic evidence.
abstract: Aphasic status epilepticus (ASE) is an uncommon manifestation of focal status epilepticus in which aphasia is the sole or predominant clinical feature. Recognition may be difficult because consciousness can be relatively preserved, convulsive activity may be absent, and the presentation can mimic acute stroke. To characterize diagnostic phenotypes of adult ASE and synthesize clinical, electrographic, and neuroimaging features across published cases. We conducted a systematic review and patient-level synthesis of adult ASE cases. Eligible patients were adjudicated as definite or probable ASE using prespecified criteria. Clinical phenotype, electroencephalographic (EEG) findings, neuroimaging, initial diagnostic impressions, treatment, and language outcomes were extracted. Ninety-nine publications contributed 168 adults with ASE, including 89 definite and 79 probable cases. Aphasia was the sole manifestation in 42.9% and predominant in 57.1%, while consciousness was preserved in 78.0%. Ictal EEG activity or electrographic status epilepticus was documented in 53.0%, and 41.7% had supportive epileptiform abnormalities. Among cases with interpretable EEG laterality, 92.7% were left-lateralized. Peri-ictal MRI abnormalities occurred in 41.2% of performed interpretable studies. Among 55 patients with interpretable functional perfusion or metabolic imaging, hyperperfusion was reported in 32. FDG-PET hypermetabolism was treated as a distinct metabolic finding. Stroke or transient ischemic attack was the most frequent reported initial impression (44.2%). Complete language recovery was reported in 77.4% of evaluable patients. Published adult ASE cases show a heterogeneous phenotype in which recognition commonly rests on concordance between language disturbance and focal EEG abnormalities, with peri-ictal imaging providing complementary evidence. These findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy of individual features or multimodal combinations.

title: Liquiritigenin attenuates inflammatory periapical bone loss by stabilizing TRIM31 and restraining NLRP3 inflammasome and cGAS-STING inflammatory signaling.
abstract: Apical periodontitis (AP) is characterized by persistent inflammation and progressive periapical bone resorption, processes increasingly associated with NLRP3 inflammasome activation and cGAS-STING-related inflammatory signaling. However, pharmacological approaches targeting these inflammatory pathways and their upstream regulatory mechanisms remain limited. Here, we investigated whether liquiritigenin, a natural flavonoid derived from licorice, attenuates inflammatory injury and periapical bone loss through TRIM31-associated regulation of NLRP3 and modulation of cGAS-STING-related signaling. Structure-based virtual screening identified several natural compounds with predicted TRIM31-binding potential, among which liquiritigenin showed the strongest protective activity against LPS/ATP-induced loss of cell viability. Pronase-protection and cellular thermal shift assays showed that liquiritigenin increased TRIM31 stability, supporting potential intracellular target engagement without establishing direct physical binding. LPS/ATP stimulation reduced TRIM31 abundance and increased NLRP3 expression, IL-1β release, cleaved caspase-1, mature IL-1β, and cleaved GSDMD. Liquiritigenin reversed these changes, whereas TRIM31 knockdown partially weakened its effects. Moreover, liquiritigenin preferentially enhanced K48-linked, but not K63-linked, NLRP3 ubiquitination; graded TRIM31 knockdown progressively reduced this response. CHX-chase and MG132 experiments further supported accelerated, proteasome-associated turnover of NLRP3. Liquiritigenin also reduced cGAMP production, STING phosphorylation, downstream TBK1-IRF3 phosphorylation, and the expression of IFN-β, ISG15, and CXCL10 under LPS/ATP stimulation. In C57BL/6 mice with LPS/ATP-induced periapical inflammatory bone loss, liquiritigenin alleviated periapical bone loss, improved micro-CT parameters, reduced inflammatory infiltration, restored TRIM31 expression, and attenuated NLRP3 accumulation and TBK1-IRF3 signaling without significantly elevating serum ALT or AST levels. Collectively, these findings identify liquiritigenin as a candidate natural compound for limiting inflammatory periapical bone loss. Its protective effects are partly associated with TRIM31-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasome-associated turnover of NLRP3 and are accompanied by attenuation of cGAS-STING-related signaling.

title: Advancing nanomaterials for treatment of eye diseases: a review.
abstract: Ocular diseases involving both the anterior and posterior segments-such as dry eye disease, keratitis, glaucoma, cataracts, diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion, and ocular tumors-remain major contributors to global visual impairment. Conventional topical and systemic therapies are limited by rapid clearance, restricted penetration across ocular barriers, and poor bioavailability, particularly for posterior-segment targets. Nanotechnology has introduced a transformative therapeutic paradigm by enabling controlled pharmacokinetics, enhanced tissue penetration, and site-specific delivery. A wide range of engineered nanomaterials-including polymeric nanoparticles, lipid-based carriers, dendrimers, metallic and metal-oxide nanoparticles, mesoporous silica systems, cerium oxide nanozymes, carbon quantum dots, nanogels, and electrospun nanofibers-has demonstrated improved drug loading, sustained release, ocular surface retention, and compatibility with biologics and gene-based agents. Emerging minimally invasive platforms, such as 4D printed smart scaffolds, dissolving microneedles and magnetically driven microrobots, further enable precise transscleral or intravitreal delivery, active navigation through the vitreous, and targeted interaction with retinal lesions. Parallel clinical advances, including FDA-approved nanoformulations and ongoing trials, confirm the translational potential of these technologies. Plus, artificial intelligence now accelerates both ophthalmic diagnosis and nanocarrier design, enabling predictive modeling of nano-bio interactions, personalized delivery strategies, and real-time disease assessment. This review integrates current advances in nanomaterial engineering and AI-guided innovation, outlining their convergent roles in shaping next-generation precision therapeutics for vision preservation and restoration.

title: Impact of Photon-Counting CT Acquisition Modes on Coronary Stenosis Assessment and Radiation Dose: A Phantom and Clinical Evaluation.
abstract: Introduction Photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCD-CT) offers high spatial resolution and dose-efficient coronary CT angiography (cCTA), but protocol selection, especially optimal acquisition mode, requires balancing spacial resolution, temporal robustness and radiation exposure. This study evaluated various PCD-CT acquisition modes in terms of image quality, blooming, stenosis grading, diagnostic accuracy, and radiation dose using phantom and clinical cCTA. Methods First-generation dual-source PCD-CT was used with four acquisition modes: high-pitch spiral with prospective ECG-gating (Flash), Sequence, Spiral, and retrospective ultra-high-resolution (UHR) spiral mode. Phantom experiments used six 3D-printed coronary artery models with stenoses ranging from 21% to 73%. In a retrospective clinical study, 41 cCTA examinations were analyzed. Qualitative and quantitative image assessments used invasive coronary angiography as reference standard for diagnostic accuracy. Patient characteristics and radiation doses were recorded. Results UHR demonstrated the highest image quality and the lowest quantitative blooming in phantom and clinical data (clinical image quality score: UHR 4.12 ± 0.99 vs. Flash 3.00 ± 0.86; p = 0.002). Diagnostic accuracy varied across protocols for detecting ≥50% and ≥70% stenoses was high across all modes (e.g., Flash: 76.5% each; Sequence: 100% and 57.1%; UHR: 64.7% and 82.4%). Radiation dose was highest in UHR (26.44 ± 9.76 mSv) compared with Sequence (13.65 ± 8.86 mSv) and Flash (1.40 ± 0.32 mSv); all p ≤ 0.011. Conclusion While UHR acquisition provides highest image quality in PCD-CT cCTA, lower-dose acquisition modes achieve comparable diagnostic accuracy for coronary stenosis detection. Protocol selection should therefore be individualized, and prospective controlled studies are required.

title: Invasive interval breast cancer rates after digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised mammography versus digital mammography screening (TOSYMA): 24-month follow-up of the multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
abstract: Background Despite high invasive breast cancer detection rates, the effectiveness of digital breast tomosynthesis screening is still uncertain. We aimed to compare the invasive interval cancer rates in women screened with digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised two-dimensional (s2D) mammography with those screened with digital mammography. Methods TOSYMA is a multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised, controlled, superiority trial done at 17 screening sites across two federal states in Germany. Women aged 50-70 years were randomly allocated (1:1) to digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography or digital mammography. The first primary endpoint of TOSYMA (TOSYMA-1) was the detection rate of invasive breast cancer and has been previously reported. The second primary endpoint (TOSYMA-2) was the invasive interval cancer rate, defined as the proportion of women who developed an invasive breast cancer in the 24-month interval after being negative at screening (ie, no ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive breast cancer detection) in TOSYMA-1. The primary endpoint was analysed in all participants with a negative screening result in TOSYMA-1. The cumulative incidence of invasive interval cancers at 12 months in screen-negative women was the prespecified secondary outcome. Suspected interval cancers were identified by data linkage to cancer registries. The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03377036) and is closed to accrual but follow-up is ongoing. Findings Between July 5, 2018, and Dec 30, 2020, 99 689 women were enrolled in TOSYMA-1 and 99 558 participants included in the modified full analysis set of TOSYMA-1. The median age was 57 years (IQR 53-62) in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set and all participants were female. 49 299 (99·1%) of 49 762 women assigned digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screened negative in TOSYMA-1, as were 49 456 (99·3%) of 49 796 women assigned digital mammography who had evaluable data and were included in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set. Invasive interval cancers were detected in 70 of 49 299 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (invasive interval rate 14·2 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 92 of 49 456 women in the digital mammography group (18·6 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0·76 [95% CI 0·55-1·06]; p=0·11). Invasive interval cancers were detected within 12 months in 22 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (4·5 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 31 women in the digital mammography group (6·3 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; OR 0·71 [95% CI 0·52-0·97]). Interpretation TOSYMA-2 indicates that about a quarter of invasive interval cancers occurring with digital mammography over 2 years might be avoided with digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screening. Although the primary outcome of TOSYMA-2 did not reach statistical significance, this large, randomised trial adds substantial evidence to the use of digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography in breast cancer screening. Funding Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (German Research Foundation).

title: Neuroimaging in the era of biologically defined Alzheimer's disease and disease-modifying therapy.
abstract: Disease-modifying therapies and biomarker-based diagnostic frameworks will fundamentally altered the clinical diagnosis and management of Alzheimer's disease. Diagnosis is increasingly anchored in the biological evidence of pathology rather than clinical presentation alone, with implications for treatment eligibility, prognosis, and monitoring. In clinical practice, patients with memory complaints can present with complex mixed pathologies that develop across the lifespan. Brain imaging, particularly MRI and PET, plays a crucial role in visualising these cumulative abnormalities. With Alzheimer's disease-specific therapies now available in many regions of the world, amyloid PET plays a central role in establishing Alzheimer's disease diagnosis, determining eligibility for amyloid-targeting therapies, and quantifying treatment-related amyloid clearance. In settings where available, tau PET informs biological stage, prognosis, and clinical heterogeneity. MRI remains indispensable for differential diagnosis, the assessment of comorbid and vascular pathology, and monitoring for complications, particularly amyloid-related imaging abnormalities. Technological advances-including quantitative imaging, artificial intelligence, accelerated acquisition, and workflow optimisation-are improving reliability, efficiency, and access to these tools. Neuroimaging is now a cornerstone of Alzheimer's disease care and a crucial discriminator tool for characterising brain injury across the lifespan. With emerging fluid biomarkers, neuroimaging supports accurate diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring.

title: Degenerative cervical myelopathy: early detection and the potential for preventing disability.
abstract: Degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM), the most common non-traumatic spinal cord injury, is a prevalent, progressive, and highly disabling neurological disease, causing heterogeneous impairment ranging from sensory loss and impaired hand dexterity to gait, balance, and autonomic dysfunction. Disability often persists despite surgical decompression, and untreated disease can progress to irreversible neurological injury, including tetraplegia. Current clinical management is largely reactive, with diagnosis and intervention typically only after neurological deterioration has become clinically apparent and radiographic evidence of cervical myelopathy is established. Advances in multimodal diagnostics over the past 5 years are now enabling the detection of subtle spinal cord injury, biological disease activity, and subclinical neurodegeneration before overt clinical disability. Quantitative spinal cord MRI, advanced neurophysiological assessments, dynamic biomechanical metrics, and sensitive functional testing provide complementary tools for early detection, risk stratification, and prognostication. Together, these approaches are redefining DCM as a disease that should be managed proactively. Evidence supports decompressive surgery in patients with moderate-to-severe disease, whereas in milder disease or in spinal stenosis that might develop into DCM, the management of patients should be interdisciplinary, with active surveillance to detect early deterioration or decompressive surgery in selected cases. Improved prediction of disease trajectories and clearer evidence on long-term outcomes could enable selective earlier intervention and help to prevent neurological disability.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of musculoskeletal ultrasound in suspected polymyalgia rheumatica: a multicentre, cohort study.
abstract: Background Diagnosing polymyalgia rheumatica is challenging, and musculoskeletal ultrasound is primarily used in diagnostically difficult situations. Previous musculoskeletal ultrasound studies in patients with polymyalgia rheumatica used case-control designs or non-representative cohorts, reducing assessment of diagnostic accuracy. This study aimed to assess the diagnostic accuracy of musculoskeletal ultrasound in two independent cohorts of patients with suspected polymyalgia rheumatica. Methods This multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study included consecutive, glucocorticoid-naive patients with suspected polymyalgia rheumatica, referred for rheumatology evaluation at the University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands (retrospective cohort), between April 30, 2019, and Feb 13, 2024, and at Aarhus University Hospital, Silkeborg Regional Hospital, and Horsens Regional Hospital, Denmark (prospective cohort), between Sept 14, 2020, and June 30, 2022. The Aarhus cohort included patients older than 50 years with proximal muscle or joint pain and excluded patients with cranial symptoms suggestive of giant cell arteritis, cancer within the past 5 years, or pre-existing inflammatory rheumatic disease. No explicit referral criteria were applied in the Groningen cohort. Participants underwent protocolised clinical examination and musculoskeletal ultrasound. The reference standard was clinical diagnosis after 6 months (Groningen) or 12 months (Aarhus) of follow-up. Musculoskeletal ultrasound assessment included subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis, biceps tenosynovitis, and hip synovitis in both cohorts, plus glenohumeral synovitis and trochanteric bursitis in the Groningen cohort. A polymyalgia rheumatica ultrasound lesion count was calculated based on six (Aarhus) and ten (Groningen) sites. Diagnostic performance of individual and combined lesions was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. There was no lived experience involvement in the study design or conduct. The Aarhus cohort study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04519580. Findings The Groningen cohort included 92 patients patients with suspected polymyalgia rheumatica (41 [45%] male, 51 [55%] female, mean age 69 years [SD 9]), of whom 58 (63%) were diagnosed with polymyalgia rheumatica after 6-month follow-up. The Aarhus cohort included 93 patients (53 [57%] male, 40 [43%] female, mean age 71 years [SD 8]), 66 (71%) of whom had a diagnosis of polymyalgia rheumatica at 12 months. No single musculoskeletal ultrasound finding was pathognomonic for polymyalgia rheumatica. The combination of musculoskeletal ultrasound findings with the highest sensitivity was the presence of at least one inflammatory lesion (Groningen: 10-site polymyalgia rheumatica ultrasound lesion count 93% [95% CI 83-98]; Aarhus: 6-site polymyalgia rheumatica ultrasound lesion count 92% [83-98]). The combination with highest specificity was the presence of at least one inflammatory lesion in both the shoulder and hip girdles (Groningen: 85% [95% CI 69-95]; Aarhus: 93% [76-99]). ROC analysis showed an area under the curve of 0·779 (95% CI 0·675-0·883) for the 10-site count in Groningen and 0·769 (0·664-0·875) for the 6-site count in Aarhus. Musculoskeletal ultrasound performed better in distinguishing polymyalgia rheumatica from non-inflammatory conditions than from other inflammatory rheumatic diseases. Interpretation Absence of shoulder and hip lesions on musculoskeletal ultrasound makes a polymyalgia rheumatica diagnosis unlikely. However, their presence requires careful clinical evaluation, as similar findings occur in other inflammatory rheumatic diseases. These findings support the use of musculoskeletal ultrasound as a potential adjunct to clinical assessment when evaluating patients with suspected polymyalgia rheumatica. Funding FOREUM, Danish Rheumatism Association, Independent Research Fund Denmark, Ketty and Ejvind Lyngsbæks Foundation, Frimodt-Heineke's Foundation, Aase and Ejnar Danielsen's Foundation, AP Møller Foundation, Health Research Foundation of Central Denmark Region, and Regional Hospital Central Jutland Research Foundation.

title: Cognitive fusion-modulated structural covariance networks predict treatment response in drug-naive OCD: A multiscale neuroimaging-transcriptomic study.
abstract: Background Cognitive fusion (CF), a core maladaptive process in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), describes overidentification with intrusive thoughts. While implicated in symptom maintenance, its neuroanatomical basis and treatment prediction utility remain poorly understood. Methods We enrolled 80 first-episode, drug-naïve OCD patients and 70 matched healthy controls. All participants underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging and clinical assessment. Patients received 8-week selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors treatment with endpoint reevaluation. Using multimodal neuroimaging, we examined group differences in gray matter volume (GMV) and structural covariance network (SCN), tested whether CF levels modulated connectivity, and evaluated baseline features for predicting treatment response. Transcriptomic analysis linked the findings to the Allen Human Brain Atlas data. Results OCD patients showed GMV reductions in frontal-limbic regions and increases in parietal/inferior frontal areas. SCN analysis revealed enhanced structural covariance within fronto-parieto-cerebellar circuits. Higher CF scores were associated with stronger structural coupling between the left angular gyrus and the right middle temporal/medial superior frontal gyri. Baseline GMV in the left dorsolateral superior frontal gyrus (SFGdl) positively correlated with CF improvement, remaining significant after controlling for overall symptom reduction. Transcriptomic analysis indicated the left SFGdl GMV patterns spatially associated with glutamatergic synapse and calcium signaling pathways. Conclusions CF in OCD links to altered structural integration between large-scale networks, with the left SFGdl emerging as a potential CF-specific treatment predictor. This multiscale study highlights combining neuroimaging with psychological constructs to understand treatment-relevant changes in OCD.

title: Structural network alterations and peripheral immune-inflammatory dysregulation define distinct subtypes of major depressive disorder with prognostic implications.
abstract: Background Immune-inflammatory dysregulation and cortical structural vulnerability have been increasingly implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, how they interact with each other, and whether immune heterogeneity in MDD is systematically organized by structural networks, remain unclear. Methods Genome-wide association studies data of MDD, gray matter volume (GMV) phenotypes, and 19 immune-related traits were utilized to assess causal relationships. A prospective cohort comprising 122 patients with MDD and 66 healthy controls underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging and assessment of 40 inflammatory and immune-related markers. Individualized structural covariance network analysis, machine-learning approaches, and survival analyses were used to identify neurobiological subtypes and evaluate treatment outcomes. Results Genetically predicted MDD was associated with lower levels of circulating IGF-1 ( p FDR = 0.013). Levels of IL-5 and leptin were negatively associated with GMV alterations in the right cingulate gyrus and bilateral putamen, respectively ( p FDR < 0.05). Structural covariance abnormalities were predominantly localized to connectivity between the default mode and limbic networks and within the limbic network in MDD, and they were classified into a hypoconnectivity subtype ( n = 49) and a hyperconnectivity subtype ( n = 73). The hypoconnectivity subtype exhibited greater anxiety and anhedonia symptoms, whereas the hyperconnectivity subtype showed broadly elevated inflammatory and immune state and achieved antidepressant response more rapidly during follow-up ( p = 0.032). Conclusions This study supports a bidirectional immune-brain framework in MDD and suggests that structure-derived subtypes classify different immune signaling heterogeneity, which may provide a biologically informed basis for stratification and prognosis in MDD.

title: Bilateral vs unilateral pleural drains in tetralogy of Fallot repair.
abstract: Objectives To compare postoperative outcomes after tetralogy of Fallot repair in patients managed with unilateral versus bilateral pleural drains. Methods In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing complete tetralogy of Fallot repair between 2020 and 2025 were included. Patients with previous complete repair, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, delayed sternal closure, or chylothorax were excluded. The primary outcome was undrained postoperative pleural effusion on routine chest radiographs. Secondary outcomes were postoperative pleural drain insertion, duration of invasive mechanical ventilation, diuretic score, ICU length of stay, and pleural drain-related complications. Multivariable regression adjusted for repair type, bypass duration, cross-clamp duration, and surgeon. Results Of 180 patients, 122 (68%) underwent unilateral pleural drain placement and 58 (32%) bilateral placement. Complex repairs were more common in the bilateral group. Undrained pleural effusion was more frequent after unilateral than bilateral pleural drain placement (42.6% vs 5.2%; p < 0.001). Postoperative pleural drain insertion was required in 9 patients (7.4%) in the unilateral group and in none in the bilateral group ( p = 0.06). Pleural drain-related complications were more frequent with bilateral pleural drains, with 4 pneumothoraces requiring intervention versus 1 self-resolving subcutaneous emphysema in the unilateral group ( p = 0.01). In multivariable analysis, bilateral pleural drain placement remained independently associated with lower odds of undrained pleural effusion, but not with duration of mechanical ventilation, diuretic score, or ICU length of stay. Conclusions Bilateral pleural drains were associated with fewer radiographic pleural effusions but no measurable short-term clinical advantage. Placement should therefore be individualised according to intraoperative findings and local practice.

title: Artificial intelligence in paediatric cardiac critical care: from predictive analytics to continuous physiologic intelligence.
abstract: Objective Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in paediatric cardiology and cardiac intensive care, where CHD, postoperative physiologic instability, and continuous bedside monitoring generate complex datasets. This review summarises current applications of artificial intelligence in paediatric cardiology and the cardiac ICU, focusing on cardiac imaging, electrocardiography, predictive analytics, waveform intelligence, and postoperative outcome prediction. Data sources A narrative review of PubMed, MEDLINE, and Scopus was performed for studies published from 2018 through 2026 evaluating artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in paediatric cardiology, CHD, congenital heart surgery, and cardiac critical care. Study selection Studies addressing paediatric or CHD-focused applications in echocardiography, cardiac MRI, electrocardiography, cardiac ICU monitoring, waveform analytics, or postoperative complication prediction were included, together with relevant reviews. Data extraction Information was extracted on study population, artificial intelligence method, clinical task, model inputs, outcomes, validation strategy, and major limitations. Data synthesis Artificial intelligence is most developed in imaging and electrocardiography, while paediatric and complex CHD evidence remains less mature. In cardiac ICU, models using electronic health record variables, high-frequency physiologic data, and risk indices have been evaluated for cardiac arrest, low cardiac output physiology, hyperlactatemia, extubation failure, and vasoactive de-escalation. External validation, prospective deployment, calibration, and workflow-safe implementation remain major gaps. Conclusions Artificial intelligence may improve diagnostic consistency, risk stratification, and early recognition of deterioration, but prospective validation and measurable clinical benefit are needed before autonomous use.

title: De Novo Design of a TROP-2-Targeting Peptide PET Tracer via AI-Guided Binding Interface Mimicry.
abstract: Trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP-2) is a transmembrane glycoprotein overexpressed across a range of epithelial malignancies, yet its clinical assessment still relies largely on invasive immunohistochemical analysis of biopsied tissues. In this study, we employed the PepMimic artificial intelligence platform to de novo design a TROP-2-targeting peptide, TR23, via binding interface mimicry, which was subsequently conjugated with DOTA and radiolabeled with 68Ga to yield the peptide-based PET probe [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TR23. The tracer bound TROP-2 with nanomolar affinity (KD = 26.8 nM), showed selective cellular uptake in TROP-2-positive cells, and exhibited high radiochemical purity (>95%) with excellent stability in saline and serum. Micro-PET/CT imaging in pancreatic (BxPC-3), prostate (PC3), and thyroid (BCPAP) xenograft models revealed rapid, specific tumor accumulation with high contrast and low background uptake, while competitive blocking studies with excess unlabeled TR23 substantially suppressed tumor uptake, confirming receptor-mediated specificity. Quantitative analysis further demonstrated strong positive correlations between SUVmax and TROP-2 expression levels verified by immunohistochemistry across all three tumor types. Collectively, these findings establish [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TR23 as a promising peptide-based PET tracer for rapid, specific, and quantitative imaging of TROP-2-positive tumors, and highlight the PepMimic-enabled strategy as a versatile platform for peptide-based probe discovery, supporting the translational potential of this tracer as a pan-cancer diagnostic agent for precision molecular imaging.

title: Preclinical Evaluation of 68Ga-Labeled Heterodimers for Dual Integrin αvβ3 and PARP1-Targeted Tumor Imaging.
abstract: Tumor heterogeneity limits the diagnostic performance of molecular imaging probes targeting a single biomarker. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and preclinical evaluation of 68Ga-labelled heterodimeric radiotracers co-targeting integrin αvβ3 and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) through a proposed "binding-anchoring" concept strategy. Conjugating the tumor-penetrating iRGD peptide with the PARP1 inhibitor niraparib and incorporating an albumin-binding moiety yielded the lead probe [68Ga] Ga-NY-Dual-IP. Molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance supported nanomolar target-binding capability of the corresponding non-radiolabeled precursors. In the 4T1 breast cancer model, [68Ga] Ga-NY-Dual-IP exhibited a tumor uptake of 7.29 ± 0.28% ID/g at 1 h, approximately 4-5-fold higher than that of the corresponding single-target probes. Cytotoxicity, haemolysis and histopathological analyses confirmed excellent biocompatibility. These findings established [68Ga] Ga-NY-Dual-IP as a promising PET probe for precise tumor imaging and potential clinical translation.

title: Mild, Fast, and General Biocatalytic Deprotection Strategies for Automated Fluorine-18 Positron Emission Tomography Radiotracer Synthesis.
abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) has become an essential tool in nuclear medicine, driving the continuous development of new radiotracers. Owing to the short half-life of fluorine-18 (110 min), radiotracer production requires fast, robust, and fully automated synthetic protocols. Reactive functional groups present on precursor molecules must be protected to prevent competition during radiofluorination, with deprotection typically achieved under harsh chemical conditions that may compromise automation and lead to partial molecular degradation. Herein, we report a general biocatalytic deprotection strategy based on porcine liver esterase (PLE) as a mild and efficient alternative to conventional chemical methods. Three protecting groups (valerate, pivaloyloxymethyl and pivaloyl ethylidene carbamate) were selected to enable the PLE-deprotection of a broad range of functional groups found in radiotracers and drugs (alcohols, phenols, carboxylic acids, amines, anilines, sulfonamides). The PivEC protective group of amines, anilines and sulfonamides was specifically developed for allowing an esterase deprotection. This approach was validated across a broad substrate scope and was successfully automated on ORA-Neptis modules for clinically relevant PET tracers, including [18F]FMISO, [18F]CABS13, and [18F]Nifene. This work establishes enzymatic deprotection as a versatile and practical strategy for PET scan application.

title: First-In-Human PET Imaging of Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A with [18F]BIBD-181: Automation, Biodistribution, Dosimetry, and Preliminary Application in Epilepsy.
abstract: We report the first-in-human evaluation of [18F]BIBD-181, a novel SV2A tracer designed with a fluoropropyl side chain to enable mild, automated radiosynthesis. A fully automated cGMP-compliant production process was developed on a commercial synthesizer, yielding the tracer with >95% radiochemical purity and molar activity >130 GBq/μmol. In eight healthy volunteers, [18F]BIBD-181 demonstrated excellent safety, rapid brain penetration peaking at 15 s post-injection, and a regional uptake pattern consistent with known synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) distribution (pallidum SUV = 2.01 ± 0.57 at 30 min). The effective dose was 2.7 μSv/MBq, with predominant renal clearance and no detectable defluorination. In pilot epilepsy patients, [18F]BIBD-181 positron emission tomography (PET) results revealed focal SV2A reductions that were confined to the epileptogenic lesionsa sclerotic hippocampus in one patient and a focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) in anotherwhereas [18F]FDG showed either extensive ipsilateral temporal hypometabolism or concordant focal hypometabolism, suggesting that SV2A imaging may offer more precise lesion delineation, particularly when [18F]FDG abnormalities extend beyond the true epileptogenic zone. These findings establish [18F]BIBD-181 as a clinically practical SV2A PET tracer with favorable dosimetry, simplified production, and promising utility for epilepsy surgical planning, warranting further validation in larger cohorts.

title: Manganese-Doped Fluorinated Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-90 for Activatable 1H/19F MRI and Metalloimmunotherapy of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: In the immunotherapy of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is substantially limited by the complex and highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Therefore, developing approaches to effectively reverse the immunosuppressive TME while enabling accurate HCC imaging poses a major unmet challenge. To tackle this critical challenge, we rationally designed and constructed a hyaluronic acid (HA)-functionalized manganese-doped fluorinated zeolitic imidazolate framework-90 (ZIF-90) nanosystem (ZM-F6@HA NPs) for integrated theranostic applications in HCC. This nanosystem not only enabled noninvasive and precise visualization of HCC lesions through GSH-activatable 1H/19F MRI for diagnostic purposes, but also induced robust tumor-associated inflammation and promoted potent antitumor adaptive immunity through synergistic mechanisms, including cGAS-STING pathway activation, immunogenic cell death (ICD) induction, and pyroptosis induction in HCC cells. The activated antitumor immune response effectively remodeled the immunosuppressive TME, and its combination with ICIs results in significant tumor regression and substantial inhibition of lung metastasis. This responsive ZIF-90-based multifunctional nanosystem provides a promising and rational strategy for integrated diagnosis and combinatorial immunotherapy of HCC.

title: Chemically Informed Artificial Intelligence Decoding of Full-Spectrum SERS Fingerprints for pH-Guided Intraoperative Assessment of Freshly Excised Melanoma Specimens.
abstract: Precise intraoperative delineation of melanoma margins remains a clinical challenge; incomplete resection causes recurrence, whereas over-excision compromises aesthetic and functional outcomes. While surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) provides chemically rich vibrational fingerprints, accurate intraoperative quantification is hindered by complex, coupled full-spectrum responses. Herein, we report a chemistry-informed artificial intelligence (AI)-SERS platform designed to support melanoma margin assessment via the detection of tumor-associated metabolic acidification. A pH-responsive HemS-SERS microarray was developed to translate the phenolic protonation/deprotonation of a hemicyanine-xanthene reporter into coordinated intensity redistributions across multiple Raman bands. Guided by this acid-base chemistry, our AI model (CIMPA-pH) encodes these pH-responsive vibrational anchors as learnable directional chemical priors, integrating full-spectrum attention with Henderson-Hasselbalch-guided prediction. This global decoding strategy accurately captures coupled pH responses, reducing prediction errors by approximately 85% and 54-78% compared to manual peak-ratio features and conventional deep-learning baselines, respectively, while a quality-control risk metric further reduces high-error readouts by 29.1%. Providing rapid (10 s) pointwise pH measurements, the platform distinguishes melanomas from normal skin with distinct pigmentation phenotypes in animal models and shows preliminary applicability for assessing melanoma-associated regions, including grossly atypical areas, in human resection specimens. Ultimately, this chemical-prior-guided SERS decoding strategy provides an interpretable framework with potential for metabolism-guided intraoperative margin assessment.

title: Optical Fiber Needle Probes for In Situ-Distributed Biosensing Based on Optical Frequency Domain Reflectometry.
abstract: In situ detection is crucial for diagnosing lesions during surgery, endoscopy, or biopsy but has always been a challenge in medical diagnostics. Optical fiber biosensing needle probes, with their small size, can be nearly noninvasively guided to the lesion site for in situ detection. However, existing optical fiber biosensing probes are single-point sensors, unable to precisely locate lesions. We propose an optical fiber needle probe for in situ distributed sensing of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) biomarker GPC3 in soft matter based on optical frequency domain reflectometry (OFDR). The needle type probe is fabricated by integrating a polydopamine (PDA)-assisted anti-GPC3 antibody-functionalized micro/nano fiber into a metal needle with a lateral opening near the distal tip. Through differential-phase demodulation, calibration experiments with varying GPC3 concentrations reveal that the needle probe exhibits an 8 mm sensing length with a sensitivity of 0.0031 rad/(ng/mL). More importantly, the proposed needle probe achieves the precise spatial localization of both independent and simultaneous multiple 250-μm mimic lesions loaded by GPC3 in an agarose-glycerol hydrogel soft matter phantom with a spatial resolution of 25 μm and a limit of detection (LOD) of 3.23 ng/mL, which offers unparalleled advantages compared with existing biosensors. The proposed method provides a potential for in situ detection and localization of HCC or other lesions.

title: Retrieval-induced forgetting and facilitation across the Alzheimer's disease continuum: Behavioral and neuroanatomical evidence from a recognition-based paradigm.
abstract: Objective The aim of the present study was to investigate facilitation (FAC) and retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF) during episodic memory retrieval across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum and to examine their gray matter correlates in verbal and visual recognition tasks. Method One hundred participants (28 AD, 29 amnestic mild cognitive impairment, 23 subjective cognitive decline [SCD], 20 healthy subjects) completed a modified retrieval-practice paradigm (mRPP) involving verbal and visual recognition tasks, a comprehensive neuropsychological battery, and 3T magnetic resonance imaging. FAC and RIF were computed at the group level and via individual proxy scores, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess the association between mRPP indices and regional gray matter volumes. Results The verbal mRPP showed reduced overall recognition in AD compared with healthy subjects ( p = .003 - η p ² = 0.23). A robust FAC effect in AD, amnestic mild cognitive impairment, and SCD was observed, whereas RIF emerged only in SCD, suggesting intact inhibitory control at the earliest stage and its disruption with disease progression ( p < .001 - η p ² = 0.48). The visual mRPP showed a strong FAC effect across all groups, with no RIF, indicating modality-specific reliance on recognition-based retrieval ( p < .001 - η p ² = 0.63). Voxel-based morphometry analyses revealed distinct gray matter correlates across groups and tasks: Verbal RIF was negatively associated with frontotemporal regions in AD patients and parieto-occipital regions in healthy subjects, while visual indices showed widespread associations with temporal, subcortical, cerebellar, and sensorimotor regions, particularly in amnestic mild cognitive impairment and SCD groups. Conclusions This study shows shared and modality-specific brain mechanisms of retrieval practice across AD stages. Preserved compensatory processes in SCD individuals give way to progressive regional disruption, supporting early, modality-tailored, and multimodal cognitive interventions to enhance cognition and delay cognitive decline. title: PET imaging enables direct evaluation of ferroptosis in HCC synergistically induced by anti-PD-L1 and Olaparib.
abstract: The efficacy of PET image-guided immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) management is limited by the lack of direct monitoring of therapeutic response. A key challenge is the mismatch between the therapeutic pathway and the imaging target, which hinders the accurate assessment of treatment outcomes. We addressed this challenge by combining anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy with Olaparib, a strategy that promotes ferroptosis in BRCA wild-type HCC by suppressing SLC7A11, thus allowing for therapeutic response evaluation via [ 18 F]FASu PET imaging of SLC7A11 expression. The combination treatment resulted in a 57% reduction in tumor volume, accompanied by decreased Ki-67 expression and increased levels of γ-H2AX and 8-OHdG. [ 18 F]FASu PET imaging revealed significantly lower SUVmax and tumor-to-background ratios in the combination group, correlating with SLC7A11 downregulation. Mechanistically, GPX4 downregulation, glutathione (GSH) depletion and elevated malondialdehyde (MDA) levels confirmed the activation of ferroptosis. Notably, no therapeutic or imaging response was observed in immunodeficient models. Thus, the SLC7A11-targeted PET tracer [ 18 F]FASu offers a clinically translatable biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy, establishing a novel theragnostic paradigm that directly evaluates treatment response via PET imaging.

title: Applications of lung ultrasound in preterm infants: implications for respiratory distress syndrome and bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
abstract: Lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a promising bedside imaging modality in neonatal intensive care units, offering real-time assessment of lung aeration without exposure to ionizing radiation. These advantages are particularly relevant for preterm infants, who are vulnerable to cumulative radiation exposure and evolving pulmonary disease. In this narrative review, we synthesize current evidence on the functional clinical applications of lung ultrasound in preterm infants. We focus on how LUS has been studied to guide early respiratory management, predict the need for surfactant and escalation of respiratory support, assess extubation readiness, identify infants at increased risk for bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and monitor disease trajectory and response to therapy throughout the NICU course, including emerging data on longer-term respiratory outcomes. While available studies demonstrate promising diagnostic and prognostic value, interpretation is limited by heterogeneity in acquisition protocols, scoring systems, timing of assessment, and operator dependence. Further multicenter studies with standardized protocols are needed to define the role of LUS in routine neonatal respiratory care.
